title: 5.2-01: Shopify client-credentials token cache keyed by shop and client id, not by connection
evidence: ingest/src/adapters/shopify/client.mjs:65,101-117 (main 35ea3e0): the cache key was shop|client id, both public values; a cache hit returned the Admin API token before the connection's own secret was read; dropToken used the same key; the jobs serve every tenant's connections in one process (core/connection.mjs:37-58). Expected from the code; unchanged since B10.
impact: A connection in another tenant naming the same shop and client id would read the shop's customers and orders into that tenant through the first tenant's token without ever holding the client secret: cross-tenant commerce data exposure class (jobs path only; webhooks stay HMAC-checked against the connection's own secret). Both tenants are the same company today, which lowers likelihood, not class.
recommendation: Key the cache by connection id, signing secret name and client id (tokenKey) in tokenFor and dropToken; README Architecture bullet and Decision log 13 Oct 2026 reworded to 'per connection (tenant and shop)'; shopify-flow and shopify-client cases.
readme_check: already open (backlog CMA-037 item 1); not in the Decision log or Open decisions

title: DB-01: Direct UPDATE of telephony_number.is_counted by the Ingest login removes a line's calls with no acting user and no permission check
evidence: Observed on the local copy as cma-ingest@local.iam with a tenant context and app.user_id empty: update cma.telephony_number set is_counted = false removed 3 calls and 1 tagging; the audit rows named actor_db_role cma_owner and no actor_user_id (db/54_uncounted_lines.sql trigger cma.remove_calls_of_uncounted_line(), SECURITY DEFINER, no assert_permission; cma_app holds UPDATE on the column by 0007a). No shipped ingest code writes is_counted.
impact: Defence in depth with a demonstrated path: a bug or injected payload in the ingest, or anyone with cma_app rights, removes every stored call of a line in milliseconds with an audit trail naming no person; recovery only by a backfill. Data-loss class, bounded to one tenant and one line per statement.
recommendation: 0008q (db/76, db/77): the trigger function asserts tenant.configure for the acting person (CMA01 without an acting user unless the owner runs it, CMA06 without the right); trigger, owner, search path and rights unchanged; verify 77 blocks A and B; 55 still passes.
readme_check: already open (backlog CMA-037 item 2); Decision log 13 Oct 2026 FIND-01 concerns the Sources screen's confirmation, not this path; the fix is additive

title: 5.2-03: Shopify read-back: one failed CRM lookup fails every unit of the batch and every retry repeats every Shopify read
evidence: ingest/src/adapters/shopify/match.mjs:87-93 had try/finally without catch, so a SourceError (rate_limited, paced, timeout, http_5xx) left the customer loop; read.mjs:233-259 turned it into crm_<code> for every pending unit, customers already matched included; the sweep's retry re-read orders, lines and customers from Shopify (backoff 2^attempts minutes, db/30:498; parked after 10 attempts). Unchanged since B10.1.
impact: Lost matches for a whole batch, up to ten times the Shopify cost and HubSpot searches for the same objects before parking, and parked events to resolve by hand; one 429 in a renewal night could park the match of every order of the run.
recommendation: Catch per customer in matchCustomers (outcome error with the code), stop further searches on rate_limited, paced or timeout, fail only the units whose customer carries an error in read.mjs; a new shopify-flow case.
readme_check: already open (backlog CMA-037 item 3); docs/ingest/README.md Shopify section described the old behaviour

title: 5.2-06: Flow verifiers defaulted INGEST_FLOW_ADMIN_USER to a real team member's address
evidence: Six ingest/verify/*-flow.mjs files (flow.mjs:42, jobs-flow.mjs:48, aircall-flow.mjs:47, shopify-flow.mjs:51, outbox-flow.mjs:39, email-flow.mjs:54) and their usage headers carried a staff work address as the default admin login (value not reproduced); a run without the variable connected as that login and failed locally with a confusing error.

recommendation: Require INGEST_FLOW_ADMIN_USER (usage message, exit 2 when unset) in the six verifiers and their headers; the docs/ingest/README.md verifiers table says to set it.
readme_check: already open (backlog CMA-037 item 4)

title: INFRA-01: A mis-configured cma-web revision passes the deploy and goes live (check-config gap plus TCP-only startup probe)
evidence: cloudbuild.yaml:33-41 check-config tested only _DATA_MODE=api without database variables and the _LOGOUT_TARGET value; the deploy step (57-69) passed no --startup-probe, so Cloud Run's default TCP probe made any listening container Ready; config.ts:25 accepted an empty IAP_AUDIENCE and iap.ts:47 refused every token per request. Observed locally on the standalone build: without IAP_AUDIENCE /api/health answered 200 while every page answered 401; with a bad CMA_AUTH_MODE the server printed Ready and every route including /api/health answered 500. Realistic triggers: a hand-edited trigger YAML (RUNBOOK 336-350) or a manual gcloud builds submit without substitutions.
impact: A successful-looking build locks every agent and manager out of the Workspace mid-shift, or serves mock data in prod, until someone rolls traffic back by hand; nothing alerts on it (INFRA-06). Same class as the 16 Oct 2026 ingest incident.
recommendation: (a) check-config validates the audience shape, refuses a mock mode without _ALLOW_MOCK=1 and checks _MAX_INSTANCES and _DB_POOL_MAX are integers; (b) --startup-probe on /api/health (CONFIG CHANGE: deploy flag only, budget unchanged); (c) /api/health answers 503 'misconfigured' when IAP_AUDIENCE is missing in iap mode or the database is not configured in api mode, with no database round trip.
readme_check: new; Decision log 5 Oct 2026 and README line 165 describe check-config for api mode only; Open decision 2017 and CMA-068 reduce how often an untested build reaches prod but do not catch a bad prod substitution
fixed_in: Pulse4all-com/cma#154 (health route); Pulse4all-com/cma#155 (check-config and startup probe)

title: WEB-01: No Content-Security-Policy on the Workspace; the first safe step is four directives
evidence: web/next.config.ts:3-9 set X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; the comment at line 3 said CSP comes with the first real data screen (shipped 5 Oct 2026); no Content-Security-Policy anywhere in web/src (observed grep); the static signed-out page has a hash-based CSP. XSS sinks in web/src: 0; every data-built href https-validated.
impact: The realistic XSS surface today is a future regression or a dependency; a CSP limits that blast radius. frame-ancestors, base-uri, form-action and object-src have no header equivalent; without form-action 'self' an injected form or base tag could redirect the Log out and Accept form posts.
recommendation: Step 1 (done): Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; object-src 'none' (sets no script-src or style-src, so it cannot break dev or prod; both form posts redirect same-origin). Step 2 (M, proposed): a per-request nonce from proxy.ts with script-src 'nonce' 'strict-dynamic', report-only first, then enforce.
readme_check: new (only the code comment at next.config.ts:3)

title: 5.2-02: No single-flight guard on the scheduled ingest jobs; overlapping executions double connections and work
evidence: ingest/src/jobs/runner.mjs:68-86 main() took no lock; no pg_try_advisory_lock anywhere in ingest/ or db/ (grep); docs/ingest/deploy.sh:229,256-258 schedules sweep, poll-forms and poll-email every minute with --tasks=1 --task-timeout=10m, and Cloud Run jobs allow concurrent executions. A sweep can exceed a minute (20 s per-call timeouts, reread, catalogs, link_calls). The claims are for update skip locked, so overlap costs resources, not duplicates. README's Database connection budget prices the worst case at +60 connections (+90 with the email poll, DOC-03).
impact: A slow vendor night stretches runs past a minute and executions pile up to the task timeout: up to ten of each at once, 60 to 90 extra connections on an instance with 97 usable, so cma-web requests fail on connection refused; double HubSpot search traffic against the account-wide 5/s limit.
recommendation: A session-level advisory lock per job name (jobLock in core/db.mjs, hashtext of 'cma-ingest:<job>') held on one pooled client for the run; a second execution logs 'skipped' with code locked and exits 0; applied to sweep, poll-forms, poll-email and reconcile; backfill and outbox stay manual; a jobs-flow case; one sentence in README's budget paragraph.
readme_check: already noted as an unguarded worst case (Architecture, Database connection budget, 15 Oct 2026); the guard itself is new

title: 5.2-04: Secret names on connection rows are not scoped to the tenant
evidence: cma.upsert_connection (db/30, db/52) checks tenant.configure and the adapter name only; signing_secret_name and token_secret_name are free text per row; cma.ingest_connection(key) and servedConnections hand the names to the one project-wide Secret Manager reader (secrets.mjs:38-48) under one service account with accessor grants on every secret (deploy.sh:153-168); nothing joins a secret name to a tenant. The peppers are the exception by construction (derived from the tenant slug). No screen exposes the field today; the writers are the runbooks in Studio.
impact: An admin of one tenant who can run upsert_connection could point a connection at another tenant's HubSpot token secret or the shared Shopify signing secret and read that tenant's CRM records into their own, or authenticate webhooks into it; the multi-tenant principle is held by who holds tenant.configure, not by the schema. Medium because no screen exposes the field.
recommendation: (a) A migration pair: an owner-maintained allow-list table cma.tenant_secret_name (RLS, setup_tenant_table) or a naming rule ^ingest-<slug>- enforced in upsert_connection and joined by cma.ingest_connection and the jobs' connection query, seeded in Studio with the names prod uses (nothing renamed in Secret Manager), a verify with a provoked row, catalog.json. (b) Until then a service-side guard refusing a secret name outside ingest-<tenantSlug>- or an INGEST_SHARED_SECRET_NAMES list (a deploy.sh env change: CONFIG CHANGE section).
readme_check: new; related settled points: secrets per named grant (15 Oct 2026), peppers per tenant slug (Architecture)

title: 5.2-05: docs/ingest/deploy.sh did not check the checkout is main, so a prod deploy from a branch shipped unreviewed bytes
evidence: deploy.sh:33 says 'on a clean checkout of main'; the only checks were git status --porcelain -- ingest (:115) and a commit touching ingest/ (:118); SHA was the branch's last ingest commit (:114), so a feature branch built ingest:<branch sha> and deployed it to prod (:191-194, :300-313); git switch main lived in the runbook text, not the script. Same class as the 16 Oct 2026 incident.
impact: Prod could run ingest code outside main (CLAUDE.md: main only accepts pull requests); a later main deploy with a coinciding sha would say 'image exists; no build'.
recommendation: After :118: refuse prod when the branch is not main (exit 2 with the switch and pull instruction), print a note for dev from a branch; verify/deploy-script.mjs inits its tree with -b main and adds two cases.
readme_check: new; Decision log 16 Oct 2026 ('a flag whose absence silently breaks prod is not optional') is the precedent

title: DB-02: The audit log writes about 3.4 rows and five copies of each webhook payload per ingest_event; cma.audit_log is the growth driver
evidence: Observed locally: ingest_event 2,934 rows against 10,022 audit rows (ratio 3.4: the insert, the claim's update, the finish's update), about 1,542 bytes of images per audit row, every update row carrying the full raw payload twice; cma.audit_log 27 MB against 3.2 MB of ingest_event. Estimated for prod from README's recorded counts: 2,000 to 3,000 events a day, 300 to 600 MB a month of audit from ingest_event alone, 0.5 to 1 GB a month in all, on a 3.75 GB instance.
impact: The audit of a technical log adds little evidence (the payload is already stored once; the transitions are deterministic) while it drives the database's growth with no retention or aggregation yet.
recommendation: (1) cma.audit_row() leaves raw out of ingest_event's images (done in 0008q, as it strips token_hash for invitation); (2) fold audit_log retention into CMA-003 and CMA-026 (processed and ignored events older than N days first; the one-year rule of 15 Oct 2026 is the ceiling); (3) later, partition audit_log by month so retention is a DROP PARTITION.
readme_check: already open (CMA-003 retention, CMA-026 aggregation; Open decisions 'Retention of staff data, the audit log and the customer-field mirror'); the five-copy amplification is new

title: DB-04: The optional-bound pattern (p is null or col >= p) kept the time indexes out of use in the report cores
evidence: cma.calls_of, cma.inbound_calls_of and cma.lead_deals_of bounded their period with (p_from is null or col >= p_from) (function bodies lines 26-27 and 31-32), which the planner cannot use as an index condition, so the (tenant, time) indexes went unused and the tenant's history was scanned for any period; README itself records 1.6 s for a month over 300,000 calls locally and 420 to 470 ms for one unbounded calls_of read (0008k). Expected from the code and README's figure; the EXPLAIN pass at synthetic volume was not completed in this run.
impact: Reports → Calls, Inbound and Speed to lead cost time proportional to the tenant's history, not the month asked, growing every month until retention exists; with no statement timeout each read also held a pooled connection for its duration.
recommendation: coalesce(p_from, '-infinity') and coalesce(p_to, 'infinity') bounds in the three cores (same rows, same signatures) and the same shape in the business_date readers; verify that results with and without bounds are unchanged and the plan shows an Index Cond.
readme_check: the symptom was documented and worked around for the history start only (0008k, 16 Oct 2026); the cause in the three cores is new

Part 2 (proposed): move the set-replace deletes (user_role, skill_level, coverage_target first) to validity columns function by function. evidence: Observed: 22 functions in schema cma with proacl null (among them open_workday, end_workday, set_status, correct_workday, correct_time_event, team_hours, team_people, user_permissions); every function from db/13 on carries explicit grants. evidence: Observed: cma.find_tenants_for_identity and cma.ingest_connection had search_path=pg_catalog, cma while the twelve other SECURITY DEFINER functions use pg_catalog, cma, pg_temp; both bodies are single schema-qualified SQL statements with no dynamic SQL, owned by cma_owner, revoked from PUBLIC.

title: DP-01: cma.telephony_raw kept string values holding an @, unlike cma.email_raw and cma.task_raw
evidence: Observed on the local database: cma.telephony_raw() of a nested payload dropped objects, arrays and a phone-shaped string but kept a key whose value was an address, because the function (db/34_telephony.sql:254-273) had no @ test; email_raw (db/68:475-495) and task_raw (db/70:83-108) drop such values. The first line of defence holds: the Aircall adapter sends a fixed allowlist of eight keys (aircall/map.mjs:33,108-114).

title: DB-11: Foreign keys without a covering index: 46 of 179, all on low-traffic paths
evidence: Observed (set-based check): 46 foreign keys lack an index whose leading columns are the key's, 24 pointing at app_user (created_by, approved_by, and so on), 4 at permission, the rest at catalogs and two from import_day; none of the referenced tables is deleted from in normal running and the page lookups have their own indexes. The one real gap was ingest_event's missing time index (DB-05).

title: DB-03: No statement timeout, lock timeout or idle-in-transaction timeout anywhere: role, pool, migrations
evidence: Observed: pg_db_role_setting holds only search_path; rolconfig null for cma_app, cma_owner, cma_readonly and the service logins; web/src/lib/db/client.ts:119-121,141-143 and ingest/src/core/db.mjs:48-60 set max, idle and connect timeouts only; no set local statement_timeout in transaction(); no lock_timeout in any migration (grep of db/*.sql). Same observation as INFRA-03 and 5.2-07.
impact: A report scanning the tenant's history held one of five pooled connections for its whole duration and was never cut; a dozen concurrent manager loads exhaust an instance's pool and every request then fails DB_UNAVAILABLE after 10 s; a daytime migration needing ACCESS EXCLUSIVE queues behind any such read and blocks every other reader and writer with no timeout.
recommendation: Web: statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout as pool options (#159); ingest: the same with a longer ceiling for jobs (#157, 5.2-07); db/76 of 0008q already starts with a lock timeout. Still proposed: README's Conventions for every migration says 'one transaction with set local lock_timeout' (DB-09), and long jobs (load_import_batch, backfill) set their own ceiling.
readme_check: new; related: Database connection budget (15 Oct 2026) counts connections, not their duration; raising max_connections stays rejected
fixed_in: Pulse4all-com/cma#159 (web pool); Pulse4all-com/cma#157 (ingest pools); Pulse4all-com/cma#151 (lock timeout in 0008q)

title: DB-05: cma.sources() ran four correlated scans of ingest_event per connection without a time index
evidence: cma.sources() (db/52) counts per connection the events of the last 24 hours, the due ones, the needs_review ones and max(recorded_at); the indexes on ingest_event were the partial (tenant, connection, next_attempt_at) for due events, the object and event-key indexes and the keys: no index on recorded_at and none covering needs_review, so three of four subqueries scanned the connection's whole event history per Sources page load. Expected from the code; not measured at volume.
impact: At 60,000 to 90,000 events a month (DB-02 estimate) the Sources page reads hundreds of thousands of rows with 1 KB payloads for four small numbers, on the page an operator opens when the ingest misbehaves.
recommendation: ingest_event (tenant_id, connection_id, recorded_at desc) and a partial index where status = 'needs_review' (both in 0008q, db/76 section 4).
readme_check: new

title: INFRA-02: cma-web's runtime settings lived in the console, not in cloudbuild.yaml; no startup CPU boost on the web service
evidence: cloudbuild.yaml:57-69 passed --region, --image, --port, --max-instances, --set-env-vars and --quiet only; gcloud run deploy keeps unpassed settings, so min-instances=1 (README 149, set by hand 12 Oct 2026), the service account, the ingress and CPU, memory, concurrency, timeout and boost were nowhere in the repository; the ingest side pins every cap in docs/ingest/deploy.sh:300-313 including --cpu-boost since 13 Oct 2026.

readme_check: Decision log 12 Oct 2026 (min-instances=1) and README 147 describe the intended state, so putting them in code is implementing; CPU boost for cma-web is new (13 Oct 2026 covers cma-ingest only)

title: INFRA-03: No statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on any pool; a few slow statements starve an instance
evidence: grep of statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction over README, db/*.sql, web/src, ingest/src and docs: nothing; pools max 5 (web, ingest service), 3 (jobs), 2 (scheduler) with connectionTimeoutMillis 10 s; pg 8.23.1 sends statement_timeout, lock_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout as session parameters at connect (no migration needed); the web request timeout was Cloud Run's default 300 s. Same observation as DB-03 and 5.2-07.
impact: Five slow statements on one cma-web instance hold all five connections; every other request on it waits 10 s then fails DB_UNAVAILABLE, clock-ins and status changes included; idle transactions pin RLS context and locks.
recommendation: statement_timeout from CMA_DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS (web default 30 s, ingest service 15 s, jobs longer through JOB_ENV: CONFIG CHANGE) and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout 30 s in both clients and the scheduler job; map SQLSTATE 57014 to a 'took too long' message through copy.ts; verify with pg_sleep through withTenant.
readme_check: new (the budget paragraph counts ceilings; nothing bounded a statement); Decision log 15 Oct 2026 (max_connections stays 100) untouched

title: INFRA-05: Parked ingest events (needs_review) have no clearing path and no Data quality row
evidence: db/30:503-504,530-532: failed events retry with 2^attempts minutes capped at 60 and park at ingest.max_attempts 10 (about four hours of a source answering 5xx, timing out or rate-limiting); sweep.mjs:1-5 never claims them again; the only surface was the eventsParked warning badge on Configuration → Sources (SourcesList.tsx:50); Reports → Data quality has outbox rows but none for parked events; no resolve function exists for ingest_event (grep; outbox_resolve exists for the outbox and has no web route either), so clearing is a Studio update by hand.
impact: After a source outage longer than about four hours, a wrong secret after a rotation or a Cloud Armor block, every event of that window parks for good: the nightly reconcile repairs objects modified since, deletions and unmodified objects stay missing, the badge never clears and nobody is told.
recommendation: (1) A Data quality row for parked events; (2) a resolve function in a migration pair (tenant.configure; needs_review to received with attempts reset for retry, or to ignored for drop; audited; provoke switch; catalog.json); (3) POST /api/v1/configuration/sources/[id]/events/resolve and a button on the Sources detail screen (copy EN and NL); (4) an alert when the parked count rises. System health (0008r) now shows parked events per connection; the resolve action and the Data quality row remain proposed.
readme_check: Decision log 9 Oct 2026 settles the parking (retry with backoff, park after 10); the clearing path and its visibility are new; the outbox's resolve (0007c) is the precedent

title: INFRA-06: One alert policy exists (cma-ingest 429); nothing watches errors, latency, job failures, the database or the certificates
evidence: docs/ingest/alert.sh:13-18,56-99 creates exactly one policy (load balancer request_count with response code 429 on cma-ingest-backend); no uptime check and no other gcloud monitoring call anywhere in docs/ or README (grep); the 14 Oct 2026 review noted the policy's creation once failed, so its presence in prod is a Browser check. The 16 Oct 2026 incident was found by people reading 401s in the request log.

recommendation: Console-only steps for Martin, dry-run first, folded into alert.sh as a table of policies with --only: 5xx share above 2 % over 5 minutes per backend; p95 backend latency (web 2,000 ms, ingest 5,000 ms over 10 minutes); failed Cloud Run job executions (3 in 15 minutes for the every-minute jobs, 1 for reconcile and the forgotten-day close); Cloud SQL CPU 80 %, memory 90 %, disk 80 %, connections above 80; uptime checks on both fronts with certificate expiry under 15 days; a log-based distribution metric on the request timing line (#159) for p95 per route.
readme_check: Decision log 12 Oct 2026 (the 429 alert) settled and kept; the rest is new; the budget alerts and CMA-034 cover cost; in-app source health is CMA-031

title: INFRA-07: Backups, PITR and HA are documented; no restore has ever been rehearsed or recorded
evidence: README 143 and 145 document daily backups with point-in-time recovery, deletion protection and regional HA; Release flow 169 says 'confirm point-in-time recovery is on'; grep of restore, clone and drill over records/, docs/RUNBOOK.md and docs/ingest/PROD_RUNBOOK.md finds no restore run; ls records/ shows no restore or drill folder. HA covers a zone failure, not a bad migration or an update without a where, which is what PITR is for.

readme_check: Release flow 169 settles 'confirm PITR'; a rehearsed restore is new

title: 5.6-01: The Live board's 10-second poll is a full page render of 8 to 9 transactions per viewer
evidence: LiveRefresh.tsx:12-19 calls router.refresh() every 10 s; live/board/page.tsx:38-60 re-runs identity plus six reads (getTeamNow 2 statements, listTeamMembersNow, getRosterToday, listSettings, getInboundNow 4 statements, getFollowUpSummary): 8 tx / 35 round trips per tick, 9 / 39 for an admin; six transactions compete for a pool of five; every render serialises about 90 KB of copy. Observed locally against the local database at seed volume: 8 transactions and 26 statements per board render, p95 62 to 69 ms. Condition for High in the area file: a measured board render above 1.6 s p95 or database time far above the 20 ms poll budget; not observed.
